t: Section 789(g)(1) (42 U.S.C. 295g–9(g)(1)) is amended by inserting before the period a comma and “$5,000,000 for the fiscal year ending September 30, 1980, $7,000,000 for the fiscal year ending September 30, 1981, and $8,000,000 for the fiscal year ending September 30, 1982”.

fable.w: This section only amends an existing provision to add authorized appropriation amounts for fiscal years 1980 through 1982. It contains no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue involving anyone outside the federal government. There is no tempting participation reading here; it is a pure funding authorization.
fable.s: is amended by inserting before the period a comma and “$5,000,000 for the fiscal year ending September 30, 1980, $7,000,000 for the fiscal year ending September 30, 1981, and $8,000,000 for the fiscal year ending September 30, 1982”.

opus.w: This section only amends a funding provision to authorize $5,000,000, $7,000,000 and $8,000,000 for fiscal years 1980–1982. It creates no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking or right to sue. The tempting reading would infer participation from the program being funded, but nothing in this text brings outside parties into a federal decision. Like Example 1, it is purely a funding provision.
opus.b:
1. **Thinking it through:** Someone might be tempted to look at what the amended section (42 U.S.C. 295g–9) covers and guess that it involves outside parties. But this amendment only adds dollar amounts to authorize funding for fiscal years 1980 through 1982. It sets up no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking or right to sue, so no one outside the federal government takes part in any decision.
